operations.specification: Implements permanent, irrecoverable deletion (hard delete) of a vote record by its unique identifier. This operation targets the 'discussion_board_votes' table, which lacks a soft-delete ('deleted_at') field. When invoked, it performs a non-reversible removal of the specified vote from the database, reflecting the absence of any soft-deletion mechanism in the schema. It is suitable for moderator or system administrator access, and any referencing/fk constraints must be handled by the backend prior to deletion. This endpoint is typically used in scenarios where a vote has been flagged as invalid, spam, or in violation of community guidelines, and the operation is expected to trigger system audit logs documenting the deletion event.
operations.description: This DELETE endpoint irreversibly removes the specified vote from the 'discussion_board_votes' table using its UUID 'id'. The operation is a hard delete, as there is no 'deleted_at' soft-delete column present. Referenced by moderators or administrators managing the integrity of voting data, it fully complies with the database schema by not referencing non-existent audit fields. Before execution, user permissions are validated to ensure only authorized actors can remove votes. Any downstream effects (such as vote counts or analytics) must rely on system reprocessing, as the vote data is permanently lost after this operation. Attempts to delete non-existent or already removed votes must return an appropriate error, such as 404 Not Found.
operations.summary: Hard delete a vote record from discussion_board_votes by ID (irreversible).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the vote to permanently delete (primary key in discussion_board_votes).

Directly operates on the 'discussion_board_tags' table, requiring at minimum a 'name' (string, unique, non-nullable). Optional fields such as 'description' (nullable string) are used for additional context. Timestamps are managed internally by the system and do not need to be supplied by the client in the request. This operation enables authorized users (usually administrators or moderators) to extend the list of tags dynamically for enhanced search and filtering.

The request body must include the 'name' property, and may include an optional 'description'. Any values for 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'deleted_at' are managed by the server, not the client. The endpoint validates uniqueness of the tag name as per the table constraint and returns an error if the name already exists. Access is restricted to authorized roles, and successful creation returns the created tag with all its fields as persisted in the database.

Optionally, it accepts 'filters' (JSON string with additional search criteria) and 'search_context' (context string such as 'thread_list'). The operation validates that the actor is a recognized system identity and persists the new search record. Only authenticated members (role: 'member') can create search history entries to maintain privacy and behavior tracking policies. operations.specification: Create a new notification in the discussion board system. This operation creates a record in the discussion_board_notifications table, which stores notification events for users. Each notification includes the recipient's member ID, the actor who triggered the event (optional), the type of notification, an optional content preview, the URL associated with the event, a read status, an optional delivery timestamp, and the creation datetime. This endpoint is utilized for events such as replies, mentions, moderation actions, or subscriptions, allowing the board to deliver user- or system-triggered notifications. Soft deletion support is present using the deleted_at field. The operation aligns with the notification requirements of the discussion board, and all fields referenced must map exactly to properties in the Prisma schema.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows the creation of a new notification record in the discussion_board_notifications table. A notification is generated whenever an action requiring user attention occurs, such as a reply to a post, a mention in a comment, the outcome of a moderation action, or a subscription event. The request body must specify the recipient_member_id (the user who will receive the notification), and can optionally include a trigger_actor_id (the user who caused the event; nullable for system messages), type (such as 'reply', 'mention', etc.), an optional content_preview for user context, a URL referencing the resource (such as a thread or comment), read status, delivered_at timestamp for delivery audit, and the created_at timestamp. The system ensures only fields explicitly present in the schema (recipient_member_id, trigger_actor_id, type, content_preview, url, read, delivered_at, created_at) are referenced.

Upon successful creation, the response is the full notification record including its UUID and all properties. If the notification is later deleted, the deleted_at field will be set for soft delete compliance.

Permission: Only authenticated members (not guests) may invoke this endpoint. Moderators and administrators may create system or bulk notifications as appropriate.

Related operations: PATCH (list with filters, often for UI inbox), GET (detail view), PUT (edit/update a notification), DELETE (soft delete the notification for audit/compliance).

Error handling: Only fields defined in the schema are accepted. Providing fields such as created_by or deleted_by, which do not exist in the Prisma schema, will yield a validation error.
operations.summary: Create a notification event record (discussion_board_notifications table).

requestBody.description: Notification creation information; must include recipient_member_id, type, url, read, created_at, with optional trigger_actor_id, content_preview, delivered_at.

responseBody.description: Details of the created discussion board notification event, mirroring discussion_board_notifications record.

This operation processes advanced search/pagination requests against the discussion_board_notifications table. The operation allows filtering by notification type, read/unread status, delivery date ranges, and supports sorting and pagination. This endpoint is intended for user inbox functionality, notifications panels, and for admin notification log audits. Only fields present in the schema (type, read, delivered_at, created_at, recipient_member_id) are to be referenced. Soft deleted notifications (deleted_at not null) are excluded from standard listings, unless specifically requested in admin audit tools.
operations.description:
Lists and filters notification events for a user. The request body can specify filters on notification type, read/unread status, delivered_at datetime ranges (for when the notification was delivered), and supports sorting by created_at or delivered_at. Pagination parameters can be provided for large notification lists. All filtering fields must correspond to fields in the discussion_board_notifications table (do not invent status fields or reference deleted_at, created_by, etc., unless they exist in the schema). Soft-deleted notifications (deleted_at not null) are omitted from standard user listings. Admins can audit the full log if their authorization allows. Results include the total count and paginated notification records.

Error handling: Providing filters on non-existent fields will result in a validation error.

This endpoint replaces legacy /inbox or /notifications views and supports both in-app and site notifications as described in the requirements analysis.

This includes the recipient, trigger_actor (optional), type, content_preview, url, read status, delivered_at (optional), created_at timestamp, and deleted_at (set only if soft-deleted; present for admin audit only). Every field returned is strictly present in the Prisma schema. Returns 404 if no such notification exists, or if it was soft-deleted unless the requester has admin audit rights.

All updateable fields are defined directly in the Prisma schema—only settable fields may be referenced. Soft-deleted notifications (deleted_at not null) cannot be updated via this endpoint.

operations.specification: Implements list-retrieval for discussion board search histories. Returns a paginated and/or filtered list of search history records. This is based on the "discussion_board_search_histories" schema, which records individual search events including actor_id, keyword, filters, search_context, and timestamp (created_at). Supports search history analytics, privacy/audit functions, and member/guest personalization. Advanced queries may filter by keyword, actor_id (guest or member), date, or context string. Pagination and sorting are required per scale/performance specifications. Fulfills requirements around audit trails, analytics, and personalized user experience.
operations.description:
This API endpoint retrieves a list of search histories stored in the "discussion_board_search_histories" table. Each record represents a search event issued by a user or guest, containing their actor_id (UUID referencing either member or guest in the discussion_board_guests or discussion_board_members tables), the search keyword, optional structured filters (as a string or serialized JSON), the context under which the search was performed (for example, thread list, homepage, or admin panel), and the timestamp when the search was issued (created_at). 

Access control must ensure that only authorized users (e.g., the associated member, a moderator, or administrator) can view a member's search history. Moderation and privacy requirements dictate that search histories are not exposed publicly and that guests can only access their own (via actor_id/session).

When performing a search through this endpoint, clients may specify pagination details (offset, limit), sorting (by created_at, keyword, etc.), or provide advanced filters (e.g., search histories containing certain keywords, or within a specific date range/context). The response should include the requested page of full history records, each with all columns defined in the schema. For privacy/GDPR compliance, no deleted or anonymized records are exposed.

The returned record includes the actor_id (UUID for member or guest who issued the search), search keyword (text), any filters used on the search (serialized string or JSON), the UI/search context string, and the timestamp of creation. 

The endpoint requires authorization—only the subject user (actor), auditors, or administrators may access this endpoint. Guests may only access their own records, verified via session. If the specified id does not correspond to an existing record, or the requesting party does not have access rights, an appropriate not found or unauthorized error is returned.

No fields that do not exist in the schema (such as deleted_at, created_by) are referenced. Returns the actual, current record with all defined properties.

It requires the client to submit the thread's UUID (discussion_board_thread_id), the author's member UUID (discussion_board_member_id), and the post body as a string. The is_edited property is always false on creation. System timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are set to the current UTC time. The operation strictly validates input: the referenced discussion thread must exist, must not be closed/is_closed, and must not be soft-deleted (deleted_at must be null). The author must be a registered, active member and not banned or suspended. If the thread is closed or deleted, creation is denied with an error. Notification and mention events may be triggered downstream, but this endpoint does not handle those side effects directly. The response includes the fully-hydrated post object for display. No soft-delete or moderation properties are generated at post-creation.

operations.specification: Search, filter, or bulk-retrieve posts for browsing, advanced search, or moderator audit. Targets the discussion_board_posts table and supports complex filtering via a request body. The operation may accept thread ID, member ID, search keywords, timestamps, is_edited, or status fields to retrieve matching posts. This enables paginated listings, moderation dashboards, or power-search UX. No unlisted fields are referenced; all filters must match actual schema, e.g., body content, created_at, deleted_at (if present). The operation should support cursor or offset pagination and allow sort order choice, returning a container with results and pagination info. Request body may extend for future filter flexibility but must match current schema.
operations.description: This PATCH endpoint provides advanced, paginated listing and searching over discussion_board_posts. Clients submit a request body object with optional filters (such as discussion_board_thread_id, discussion_board_member_id, is_edited, keyword on body, created_at range), pagination parameters (page, pageSize, cursor), and sort order requirements. The system returns matching posts (excluding ones with deleted_at set) along with total counts and pagination cursor or page meta. This is used for rendering thread post lists, searching for specific posts, moderator audits, or analytics. The search only filters on fields present in the schema and never on inferred/calculated fields. Input validation ensures bad filters result in errors. Unauthorized users cannot access non-public posts. The response always includes a listing structure with post objects and meta.

operations.specification: Retrieve the full detail of a single post record by its unique identifier (UUID). The operation queries the discussion_board_posts table and returns the complete post entity, including its relationships (thread ID, member ID), core content, timestamps, and moderation state such as is_edited. The response must not fabricate fields and must reflect the current DB state. If the post has been soft deleted (deleted_at), it should not be returned to unauthorized users. Attempts to fetch a non-existent or unauthorized post lead to error responses. This operation forms the basis for detail/moderation popups and direct-link navigation to posts.

Access control logic ensures the user is allowed to view: deleted posts are only accessible to moderators; regular members see only active posts. Fetch errors for invalid IDs or insufficient permissions generate error responses. The returned object matches the schema exactly, with no extraneous fields. Used in direct-link views and audit traces.

operations.specification: Update a post by its UUID. This operation targets the discussion_board_posts table, accepting a request body with fields to update: body (content), is_edited (must be set to true upon edit), and possibly updated_at. The schema does not include any soft/hard delete logic here. Validates that the post exists and is not deleted (deleted_at must be null), and that the user is the post author or a moderator/administrator. Edits to body content are allowed only for authorized users. System automatically updates the is_edited flag to true if an edit occurs and sets updated_at to the current timestamp. Returns the updated post object reflecting all new state.

Permitted fields for update include 'body' (the main content), and the is_edited field is forcibly set to true when editing occurs. The operation is denied if the post does not exist or has been soft-deleted (deleted_at set). It validates user permission: member must be the author, or be an escalated moderator/admin. On update, updated_at is set to the present timestamp. The response includes the up-to-date post object. Operations that attempt changes to non-existent or deleted posts result in an error. The operation does not support hard-deletion or content restoration; those are handled elsewhere.

If already deleted or missing, responds with error. Event is logged for moderation trail. Hard delete is never performed by this endpoint.
operations.description: This endpoint issues a soft deletion for a post by setting deleted_at in the discussion_board_posts record. The endpoint never erases the row physically (hard delete), strictly following the presence of the deleted_at field. Attempting to soft-delete an already deleted or non-existent post results in an error with reason. The operation checks the author's identity or moderator/admin status before allowing the soft delete. The event is always written to the moderation log. This endpoint does not recursively soft delete child comments or attachments.

The file_uri points to the external storage location (not raw data). Optional deleted_at for future soft-deletes; the operation does not perform deletion here. The operation checks for hash duplicate prevention, file size/extension policies, ensures the referenced parent record and member exist and are valid, and then inserts the attachment row. Returns the attached file record, including all IDs, timestamps, and moderation flags. Deleted_at is never set here (not a delete).

IDiscussionBoardSubscription.description:
Represents a subscription relationship in the discussion board platform. This entity stores a user's (member's) subscription to a target resource, which enables them to receive notifications regarding updates or activity related to that target (such as threads, sections, tags, etc.).

This model enforces a normalized, atomic linkage between the subscriber and the subscribed resource. It is crucial for supporting the platform’s notification and alerting mechanisms as described in the requirements analysis. The schema enforces uniqueness for (member_id, target_type, target_id) to prevent duplicate notifications and manage resource-follow logic efficiently.

id.description:
Primary key. Uniquely identifies each subscription record. Used for all update, delete, and detail operations referencing a subscription.

This is a randomly generated UUID, ensuring global uniqueness.

member_id.description:
Foreign key to the subscribing member (discussion_board_members.id). Indicates which user is following the resource for notification or activity tracking purposes.

Required. Used highly in filtering and subscriber personalized dashboards.

target_type.description:
The type of resource being followed/tested. For example, 'thread', 'section', 'tag', etc. This value is used to drive polymorphic notification logic.

Atomic and required for filtering, usability, and context-driven subscription delivery.

target_id.description:
The ID of the actual resource being followed (thread, section, tag, etc.). Its meaning is interpreted in conjunction with target_type.

Required. Used for notification dispatch and resource update queries.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the subscription was created.

Required for audit logging, time-based filtering, and administrative oversight.

IDiscussionBoardSubscription.IRequest.description:
Request model for querying or paginating subscription records for the discussion board. This allows filtering by member ID, target type, target ID, and time ranges. Also includes support for pagination fields (page, limit) to enable scalable listings for UX and admin. Used in PATCH and search endpoints.

All filter fields map directly to schema fields and support advanced admin/member content management workflows.

member_id.description:
Optional filter. The subscribing member for whose subscriptions we want the list.

Use this for personalized settings or audit retrieval.

target_type.description: Optional filter. Type of resource being followed, e.g., 'thread', 'section', 'tag', etc. Used for filtering specific types of subscriptions in dashboards.

target_id.description: Optional filter. ID of the resource being followed (thread, section, tag, etc.), used to check if the member is following a particular entity.

page.description: Optional. Page number for pagination. Used in paginated API responses to enable scalable UX/admin dashboards.

limit.description: Optional. Amount of records to display per page for pagination. Used in scalable listings for admin/member operations.

IPageIDiscussionBoardSubscription.description: Paginated container for discussion board subscriptions. Used to return listing results for PATCH/list APIs. Contains page metadata and an array of subscription records according to the request.

data.description: Array of subscription records matching the filter/search context. Each element is an IDiscussionBoardSubscription entity.

IDiscussionBoardSubscription.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for subscriptions in the discussion board. Allows changing what resource the subscription is for (target_type/target_id) and to transfer ownership (member_id) if business logic requires.

All properties are optional to allow PATCH semantics, and only schema-defined properties are included.

member_id.description: Foreign key to member. Update this to transfer the subscription to another user. Normally used only in rare admin workflows.

target_type.description: Target type of subscription (e.g., 'thread', 'section', etc.). Changing this shifts the type of notification scope. Used in admin correction or rare legacy migration workflows.

target_id.description: The new resource to be subscribed; must reference a valid existing ID for the indicated type.

IDiscussionBoardMention.ICreate.description:
Creation DTO for a mention event (‘@mention’) on the board. Each instance signals an actor (the mentioning member) referencing another member within a post, comment, or thread. This enables notification delivery and mention analytics as described in the requirements.

This model requires all reference fields so that notifications are contextually correct.

mentioned_member_id.description: The ID of the member who is being mentioned (target of the mention). Required for mention resolution and notification delivery.

actor_member_id.description: The member who performed the mention action. Required for context/audit and UX features like “show mentions by this user”.

content_type.description: Indicates in what context/content the mention occurred (e.g., 'thread', 'post', 'comment'). Used to resolve the linked object for notification routing.

content_id.description: ID of the post, thread, or comment where the mention was made. Ensures direct linking in notification UI and audit.

created_at.description: Timestamp (UTC/ISO 8601) of when the mention happened.

IDiscussionBoardMention.description:
Schema representing an @mention event in the board. Used in notifications logic and analytics. This entity directly maps to discussion_board_mentions in the schema and is critical for driving user awareness of threaded/nested references by other members.

Each mention contains full linkage to both originator and recipient, along with the exact content context where the mention occurred. The model is immutable after creation in the normal course of business (admin-only updates/corrections permitted).

id.description: Unique identifier for the mention event, as assigned by the database sequence.

mentioned_member_id.description: UUID of the target member who was mentioned in the content.

actor_member_id.description: UUID of the member (the actor) who mentioned the target; used in notification and activity reporting.

content_type.description: What type of resource the mention was made in (e.g., 'post', 'comment', 'thread'). Used by notification ir routing logic.

content_id.description: UUID of the specific content instance where the mention occurred.

created_at.description: The UTC timestamp when the mention event occurred in the system.

IDiscussionBoardMention.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for advanced mention event searching/filtering. All filter fields correspond to the atomic schema-level fields. Used to drive UX dashboards for mentions, admin panels, or notification/analytics features. Fields may be combined. Pagination support enables scalable reporting.

Includes all atomic mention reference fields and pagination controls.

mentioned_member_id.description: Optional. Filter by target member. Used to get mentions received by a user.

actor_member_id.description: Optional. Filter by actor. Used to get mentions made by a user.

content_type.description: Optional. Restrict by entity type: 'post', 'comment', 'thread', etc.

content_id.description: Optional. Restrict to mentions in a specific resource instance (matches schema’s content_id field).

page.description: Pagination: which page to load (optional).

limit.description: Pagination: maximum records per page (optional).

IPageIDiscussionBoardMention.description: Paginated container of @mention records, used in mention dashboards and analytic queries. Every record is a full IDiscussionBoardMention, paired with standard pagination metadata for UX, admin, or reporting scalability.

data.description: Actual array of mention events for the current page.

discussion_board_mentions.description:
The base model mapped 1:1 to the discussion_board_mentions table, used in detail retrieval scenarios and direct foreign key resolution. This is identical to IDiscussionBoardMention, but defined for reference consistency.

Each record represents a persistent mention event and includes all atomic reference and audit fields from the schema.

id.description: Unique event ID. Used internally for referential integrity and lookup.

mentioned_member_id.description: Member who was mentioned (target of notification, foreign key to discussion_board_members).

actor_member_id.description: Member who performed the @mention (foreign key to discussion_board_members).

content_id.description: Resource instance where the mention occurred (thread/post/comment).

created_at.description: Creation timestamp for the mention, used in notifications and audit.

discussion_board_mentions.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for discussion_board_mentions; generally used only by admins for correction of wrong/duplicate data. All properties are optional. Enables rare mutation scenarios for referential realignment or data correction after-the-fact.

mentioned_member_id.description: Target member for the mention, updated for correction workflows.

actor_member_id.description: Updated source actor if original was wrong or migrated.

content_type.description: Corrected type value for context, e.g., to fix misattributed mention context.

content_id.description: Replacement content instance UUID (should match the referential resource).

discussion_board_vote_types.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new vote type (e.g., upvote, downvote, like, etc.) in the system's dictionary of voting actions. Each record must include code (unique string), name (display string), optional description, and required timestamps are set by the system.

Enables admins to define or extend valid voting types for actions on content. All properties other than description are required.

code.description: Short, unique code for the vote type (e.g., 'upvote'). Used for programmatic references in voting logic.

name.description: Human-readable string for display (e.g., 'Upvote'). Enables clear UI/UX references.

oneOf.description: (Optional) Description of what this vote means (e.g., 'Indicates positive reaction to content.'). Enables admin annotations and system documentation.

description.description: (Optional) Description of what this vote means (e.g., 'Indicates positive reaction to content.'). Enables admin annotations and system documentation.

discussion_board_vote_types.description:
Represents a voting action type in the board (e.g., upvote, downvote). Each type is referenced by all votes that record a user's preference on threads, posts, or comments.

The schema normalizes allowed actions for system-wide and UX consistency, audit, and analytics. Fields and behaviors are explained in the table-level documentation (see voting/analysis requirements for full business logic).

Timestamps for creation and update support audit, management, and analytics workflows.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the vote type record, mapped 1:1 to DB row.

code.description: Short, unique code (see ICreate), e.g., 'upvote', used by system logic to distinguish voting semantics.

name.description: Human-readable name of the vote action for display in interfaces.

oneOf.description: Optional. Administrative or UX-facing hint annotation to describe business meaning or voting policy.

description.description: Optional. Administrative or UX-facing hint annotation to describe business meaning or voting policy.

created_at.description: When the vote type was created in the system (ISO 8601 UTC timestamp).

updated_at.description: Timestamp for last update (required by DB for referential and audit consistency).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Page information for paginated result sets. Contains the current page, limit per page, and total statistics. Used by IPage<T> containers.

Crucial for all listing, search, or dashboard APIs.

limit.description: Number of records per page (page size). Default is 100.

records.description: Total number of records matching the search/filter query.

pages.description: Total number of available pages based on records and limit (rounded up).

전체 데이터 수, 현재 페이지 번호, 페이지당 표시 개수, 전체 페이지 수 정보를 포함하며, IPage<T>의 pagination 필드로 사용됩니다.

page.description:
The page number for pagination. Optional but recommended for large datasets. Must be a positive integer. For administrative and user list/browse operations.

Aligns with standard IPage.IRequest pattern from the requirements analysis for API pagination and search.

limit.description:
Limit of records per page. Defaults to 100 if not specified (see IPage standard). Must be a positive integer.

Controls batch size for queries, helping to avoid excessive resource use during large search, list, or bulk fetches.

title.description:
Thread title (partial or full match), for advanced filtering. Enables search/browse APIs to filter threads by their titles as required by full-text search features (Requirements: Feature 2.4, advanced search). Can be used for substring or fuzzy matching in UI.

discussion_board_category_id.description:

is_pinned.description:
Filter on whether the thread is pinned. Used by moderation/admin panels and for UI UX (see Feature: Moderation Tools). Optional.

References 'is_pinned' in the thread schema.

is_closed.description:
Filter for open/closed threads. Useful for moderation, thread lifecycle management, and user experience flows. Optional.

References 'is_closed' in thread schema.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time to filter by thread creation time (range or specific). Supports time-based filtering, archival, and administrative review as outlined in non-functional requirements.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time to filter by thread update time (range or specific). Supports activity, modification tracking, and audit compliance.

oneOf.description: Used to include or exclude soft-deleted records in searches. If set, only returns records marked deleted via soft deletion for full moderation panel compliance. Null or unspecified by default to exclude deleted items. Relates to audit, compliance, and reversibility features.

IDiscussionBoardThread.IRequest.description:
Request object for searching, paginating, and filtering discussion threads.

References: 'discussion_board_threads' table in Prisma schema and requirements analysis (Features: Thread & Post Creation, Moderation, Search).

Contains standard pagination (page, limit) and all filterable top-level thread properties. Enables admins and moderators to perform complex filtered searches, as well as end-users to find relevant discussions.

All fields align with actual columns in the Prisma table.

See IPage* pattern for pagination container and Feature 2.4 (Browsing & Search) for business rules.

data.description: Array of thread records for the current page, each matching the thread schema.

IPageIDiscussionBoardThread.description:
Pagination container for lists of threads, as per IPage<T> standard interface.

The 'pagination' property provides total count, current page, limit, and other cursor meta as required by the requirements document and standard API practices.

The 'data' field is an array of IDiscussionBoardThread records (matching the thread object as defined by the schema).

This component allows APIs to deliver paginated, consistent, and predictable thread list responses for both UI and programmatic querying.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the thread. UUID as primary key, generated by the DB. See 'discussion_board_threads.id' in Prisma schema table. Required for all entity references and for linking in UI and API layers.

Business: Used as thread URL slug and for resource updates.

discussion_board_member_id.description: UUID of the member (user) who created the thread. Fulfills relationship and moderation logging needs per schema and requirements analysis. Not directly mutable except by DB/business logic.

discussion_board_category_id.description: UUID for the master category of the thread (foreign key relation). Used for both search and detailed inspection as required by the requirements and ERD. Not mutable after assignment except by explicit admin workflows.

title.description: Descriptive title for the thread. Cannot be null. Required by the thread creation and browsing flows. See requirements Features 2.1, 2.4 for search/discovery.

body.description: Full body content of the opening message (root post) for the thread. This is distinct from post replies, and is always present. See Features 2.1 and 2.2 for business logic/UX.

is_pinned.description: Indicates if thread is currently pinned (featured/top of list in UI). Used in moderation and admin workflows. True for high importance/reference threads. Settable by moderators/admins.

is_closed.description: True if the thread has been closed by moderator or admin, and no further posts are permitted. Enforces locked-topic state as per requirements. Used in moderation dashboards.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for thread creation. Required for audit, sort, and compliance. See 'discussion_board_threads.created_at' in schema.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for last update to the thread (title, is_closed, etc). Required for compliance and admin audit. See 'discussion_board_threads.updated_at'.

oneOf.description: If set, indicates a soft delete (hidden from most users). Required for reversibility and compliance (see requirements: audit trail, Feature 2.3, moderation). Not usually shown in end-user UX unless full audit record is needed.

If set, indicates a soft delete (hidden from most users). Required for reversibility and compliance (see requirements: audit trail, Feature 2.3, moderation). Not usually shown in end-user UX unless full audit record is needed.

deleted_at.description: If set, indicates a soft delete (hidden from most users). Required for reversibility and compliance (see requirements: audit trail, Feature 2.3, moderation). Not usually shown in end-user UX unless full audit record is needed.

IDiscussionBoardThread.description:
Full entity object for a discussion board thread, matching all fields in the Prisma schema's discussion_board_threads table.

Includes all properties: id, category and member linkage, title, pinned/closed state, full content, and audit timestamps (creation, update, deletion).

This is the central/top-level entity for discussions, as described in requirements Section 2 (Features & User Journeys). Used for detail views, thread lists, and programmatic introspection across API layers.

All IDs are UUIDs for consistent global linking and relationship representation.

Security: All response types must omit any actor authentication or sensitive PII that are forbidden by platform policy. Only public-facing system attributes included.

title.description: New title string for the thread. Updating this field allows a moderator or admin (as well as original author, if policy allows) to change the display label. Cannot be set to null.

body.description: Updates the body content of the root thread post (opening statement). Use for corrections, moderation, or author revision. Cannot be null.

is_pinned.description: Allows pinning or unpinning a thread. True to pin, false to unpin. Moderators/admins only. Optional in update.

is_closed.description: Allows closing (locking) or reopening a thread for further posts. True to close (lock), false to reopen. Moderators/admins only. Optional in update.

discussion_board_category_id.description:
Update the category (taxonomy) of the thread. Only administrators or moderators may alter this value in most use-cases. Optional in update.

References the discussion_board_category_id FK in the schema.

IDiscussionBoardThread.IUpdate.description:
Data for updating a thread (discussion_board_threads) entry. Only mutable fields are present, and per compliance, 'id', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'deleted_at', and creator links are not settable. Update payload may contain any subset of mutable fields, as allowed by business logic and API permissions.

References Prisma schema 'discussion_board_threads' and requirements doc for update workflow (Feature 2.1 and moderation tools).

Used in PUT/PATCH requests for thread editing.

success.description: Indicates if deletion was successfully completed (soft deletion). True if deleted_at was set, false otherwise.

message.description: User-facing message or error string indicating result. Used to confirm success or explain why operation failed (e.g., not found, already deleted, permissions issue.

thread.description: Thread object as it exists after the deletion event is processed. Includes all properties, with deleted_at set if deletion occurred, or original state if not.

IDiscussionBoardThread.IDeleteResult.description:
Result object for soft delete operation on a thread. Delivers operation status, message, and updated thread entity object as per deletion compliance and audit rules. Required for client, moderator, and admin confirmation flows.

References requirements doc on soft delete reversibility, moderation workflows.

discussion_board_thread_id.description: ID of the thread to which this post will belong. References the parent thread (discussion_board_threads.id) as per ERD and business logic. Required for all post creation events.

discussion_board_member_id.description: UUID of the member creating the post. This is the authenticated actor (see security requirements: must be derived from authentication context, NOT client-provided for POST; included here for administrative/impersonation scenarios only as per API variant. For typical end-user flows, the system populates the member_id from session.

body.description: Main content string for the new post. Required. Used for discussion continuation, arguments, questions, or insights. See requirements doc for content posting logic. Cannot be empty/null.

IDiscussionBoardPost.ICreate.description:
Object for creating a new post in discussion_board_posts as per Prisma schema and requirements doc. Used in POST endpoint for new posts (replies/continuations in threads). Contains references to parent thread, author (member), and required body content.

Security: Systems must not allow arbitrary member_id; API must validate that the value matches authenticated context. For admin or moderation flows, member_id may be set for impersonation, but not in public endpoints.

id.description: Unique identifier for the post (primary key, UUID per Prisma schema). Required for reference, linking, and object-level access.

discussion_board_thread_id.description: UUID for the thread this post belongs to (foreign key). Required, not nullable. For navigation, thread aggregation, and parent-child relationship mapping.

discussion_board_member_id.description: UUID for the member (user) who authored the post. Set by the system, not mutable by client after creation (see Requirements Analysis security notes).

body.description: Full content string for the post. Always present; never null. Source for thread continuity, arguments, or information sharing.

is_edited.description: True if post was edited after creation. Required for audit trail and edit-tracking flows (see moderation requirements).

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for creation (Prisma 'created_at'). Used by UI and compliance.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for last modification (edit/audit trace). Required in all responses.

oneOf.description: If present, indicates post is soft-deleted (hidden from most users but kept for compliance and reversibility).
If present, indicates post is soft-deleted (hidden from most users but kept for compliance and reversibility).

deleted_at.description: If present, indicates post is soft-deleted (hidden from most users but kept for compliance and reversibility).

IDiscussionBoardPost.description:
Discussion board post object, matching all atomic fields in Prisma discussion_board_posts. Key relational and business properties are included.

Never contains sensitive authentication or role escalation fields, in accordance with the requirements doc. Used in thread display, moderation logs, and post listings.

All relationships are strict UUID references for traceability and link navigation.

page.description: Page number in paginated listing (see IPage.IPagination). Used for controlling fetch window. Optional, defaults to 1 if unspecified. Required for client-driven pagination.

discussion_board_member_id.description: Optional filter for posts authored by a specific member (user). Used in profile views, moderation, and analytics. Null or omitted for all posts in thread.

body.description: Keyword filter for contents of body. Enables admin UI, moderator search, or advanced relevance feeds. Nullable/optional.

created_at.description: Start of created_at date-time range for query (ISO 8601). Used for analytics, range queries, and moderation UX.

oneOf.description: If set, includes/excludes soft-deleted posts for audits/editorial review. Null or omitted for active-only filtering.
If set, includes/excludes soft-deleted posts for audits/editorial review. Null or omitted for active-only filtering.

deleted_at.description: If set, includes/excludes soft-deleted posts for audits/editorial review. Null or omitted for active-only filtering.

discussion_board_post_id.description: ID of parent post to which this comment is attached (see ERD and requirements). Required for root comment creation.

oneOf.description: Optional UUID of parent comment (for nested/threaded replies). Null for root-level comments or single-level replies. Enables UI threading and moderator audits. See requirements on deep discussions.
Optional UUID of parent comment (for nested/threaded replies). Null for root-level comments or single-level replies. Enables UI threading and moderator audits. See requirements on deep discussions.

body.description: Content of the comment (cannot be null/empty). Required for discussion and engagement. All business, moderation, and audit UX is built on this property.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description: Object for creating a comment on a discussion board post (discussion_board_comments). Contains all required fields (post ID, member ID, body) and optional parent for threading. Strictly follows Prisma schema and security guidance from requirements: member_id must be the authenticated actor.

Primary Key. Unique identifier for the comment entry.

As described in the Prisma schema for discussion_board_comments: Uniquely identifies each comment for reference, audit, and business logic purposes.

discussion_board_post_id.description:
Parent Post's {@link discussion_board_posts.id}. Links this comment to the post it references. Required and non-nullable as defined by the schema.

This is critical for correct threading of discussions and the integrity of content association (Prisma schema: 'discussion_board_post_id String @db.Uuid').

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Discussion Board Comment Entity

This type fully represents a comment entry in a political/economic discussion board platform, as normalized in the discussion_board_comments Prisma schema (see database design and requirements analysis §3, F03, F04, F08).

- Used for allowing members to add commentary to posts, supporting both direct and nested/threaded replies (through parent_id).
- Tracks full audit lifecycle with timestamps and edit/delete flags for transparency, compliance, and moderation history.
- Strict ownership linkage between content and discussion_board_member_id, supporting attribution, moderation, and notification.
- Maintains referential integrity to parent post and, optionally, a parent comment, enabling complex discussion structures.
- Fields and constraints fully conform to 3NF and requirements for traceable, auditable, and reversible content management without leaking any sensitive or non-attributed business data.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this moderation log record. This value serves as the primary key in the moderation logs table for the discussion board moderation domain. Automatically generated by the system at log creation. Reference: See 'id' in the Prisma schema for discussion_board_moderation_logs.

Serves for direct reference in audit trails, compliance checking, and API lookups. Must be present and unique for every moderation event record.

moderator_id.description:
UUID of the moderator who performed this action. Required. This foreign key references the moderator in the discussion_board_moderators table.

Business use: Identifies who enacted the moderation action, maintains role traceability, and ensures mod actions are auditable and not spoofed. Must always reference a valid, active moderator at the time of the event.

oneOf.description:
ID of the discussion thread involved in the moderation action, if relevant. Nullable: if the action is not directly tied to a thread (possible for cross-thread or non-article-level actions), this should be null.

Reference: 'thread_id' in the Prisma schema. Used for filtering/moderator dashboards and audit traceability, allowing reversibility and restoration at the thread level.

oneOf.description:

Useful for precise undo/redo, drill-down popups, and context navigation during issue tracing/audit reviews.

Advances auditability, supports forensic analysis for deeply-nested discussion threads, and fine-grained analytics on comment-level moderation patterns.

action.description:
Atomic action string indicating the moderation operation taken. Examples: 'hide', 'delete', 'warn', 'edit'. Always required, never nullable. See 'action' in the Prisma schema for discussion_board_moderation_logs.

Drives compliance reporting, moderator analytics, and user-facing complaint or warning presentation. Ensures each event has a machine-readable event code.

oneOf.description:
Optional textual description or rationale provided at the time of moderation. Used for transparency in audit logs and user-facing moderation explanations. Reference: Prisma column 'action_reason' (nullable).

May include business justification, cited policy violations, or moderator notes; useful for internal and external audits, dispute handling, and escalation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this moderation log entry was created. Required—automatically captured at the time moderation was performed. Adheres to ISO 8601 format, UTC.

This value is referenced in chronologically sorting audit dialogs, reconstructing issue escalations, and platform-wide compliance reporting. See 'created_at' in discussion_board_moderation_logs Prisma model.

IModerationModerationLog.description:
Moderation Audit Log Entity

Represents a single immutable moderation action taken by a moderator in the discussion board system. This entity logs all audit attributes for compliance—who performed what action on which resource (thread, post, comment), the rationale for action, and when it took place. Ensures full business and regulatory traceability for every moderation event, as per requirements analysis and non-functional security/audit controls.

Reference: Prisma schema 'discussion_board_moderation_logs'.

Every property maps to an atomic database column, no derived or denormalized fields present. Used throughout moderation dashboards, audit trail popups, compliance exports, and system-wide analytics. Relationships provided by ID FKs allow drill-down, reversibility, and cross-entity tracing.

operations.specification: Create a new discussion board channel. This operation adds a new row to the discussion_board_channels table, which is designed to support channel partitioning and top-level forum division (e.g., 'Politics', 'Economics'). Required fields are: code (unique), name, description (optional), created_at, updated_at. Soft deletion is supported via the deleted_at field for reversibility and audit trails. Only fields defined in the schema will be referenced. Unique constraints on code are enforced at the database level. Permissions: typically administrator or moderator role.
operations.description: This operation allows system administrators or moderators to create a new discussion board channel by supplying a unique code, a human-readable name, and an optional description. The request body must include these fields (except for deleted_at, which is set by system on soft deletion). The API enforces normalization as described in the Prisma schema: code and name are atomic, and unique constraints on code protect routing integrity. Upon creation, the created_at and updated_at timestamps are required by the DB for audit purposes. If an attempt is made to use a duplicate code, a unique constraint error will be thrown. The new channel is available for association with sections and further discussion partitioning immediately. All business logic assumes only schema-defined fields—deleted_at is set to null on create. Moderation and admin APIs including audit trailing make use of these attributes for further actions or reversibility. System must not accept additional fields not in schema. Soft delete (not hard delete) is supported for this entity through deleted_at, but not part of the create operation itself.
operations.summary: Create a new channel entry in the discussion_board_channels table.

requestBody.description: Information for creating a new channel. Must include code (unique), name, and can include description.

responseBody.description: Information about the newly created channel, as stored in the discussion_board_channels table.

operations.specification: Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of discussion board channels from the discussion_board_channels table. This operation supports both full listing and advanced search/filtering for administrators or moderators. Soft deleted entries (deleted_at set) can be included or excluded based on request, but the endpoint references only actual schema fields. All fields for filtering/sorting/searching must match the schema: code, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. The endpoint uses request body for complex search parameters and returns paginated results for audit/admin viewing.
operations.description: This operation supports complex search and retrieval of discussion board channels for administrative views. It enables searching, filtering, and paginating channels based on code, name, description, created_at, updated_at, or inclusion/exclusion of soft-deleted channels (based on the deleted_at field, which, if set, marks a channel as deleted). Requests must only reference schema fields for both input and output; any search or sort must reference code, name, description, created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at. Filtering by code or name supports rapid navigation, while pagination supports administrative scalability. All returned fields in each channel in the response strictly reflect schema attributes—no extra fields are inferred or available. Responses exclude or include soft-deleted records based on the request body parameters. System audit and moderation tools use this endpoint for channel review, restoration (via a separate endpoint), or audit trailing. The page structure includes total count and data array, with each array element matching the channel schema.
operations.summary: List and search discussion_board_channels with pagination and filtering.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination criteria for channels. All filterable fields must exist in schema: code, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

responseBody.description: Paginated response of channel records matching criteria. Each record matches the channel schema fields.

operations.specification: Fetch a single discussion board channel's detailed data from the discussion_board_channels table, using its unique ID. This operation returns all schema-defined fields for a channel, including code, name, description, created_at, updated_at, and soft deletion timestamp (deleted_at). The ID must match an existing row; if not found, a not-found error will be returned. Only schema fields are included in the result.
operations.description: Retrieves all information for a single discussion board channel, identified by its UUID (id), from the discussion_board_channels table. This includes code, name, description, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. If the channel is soft deleted (deleted_at is not null), that fact is included, but soft-deleted channels may or may not be returned based on administrative policy. The operation does not return fields that are not part of the schema. This fetch supports administrative and moderation dashboards in reviewing or editing channels as well as fetching for content partition navigation. Not-found errors result if the id is not present in the database.
operations.summary: Get details of a specific channel from discussion_board_channels by id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique id of the channel to fetch (must be a UUID matching a row in the discussion_board_channels table).

responseBody.description: Channel record as defined in schema, or not found error.

operations.specification: Update one discussion board channel (by id) in the discussion_board_channels table. The operation supports updating schema fields: code, name, description. Updates automatically set the updated_at timestamp to now. Only schema fields are modifiable; any extra fields or attempts to update created_at or deleted_at will be ignored. Unique constraint on code is enforced. Returns the updated record.
operations.description: This operation updates a channel's attributes—code, name, or description—using the provided id. The request body may optionally contain any of these updatable fields. The updated_at timestamp is always automatically set by the system to the current time upon update. Only fields present in the schema (code, name, description) are updatable; attempts to update non-schema fields will result in errors or ignored values. If the code is updated to a value that already exists for another channel, a unique constraint error will occur. The operation returns the updated channel, as defined by the schema, including all current values of its fields. The deleted_at value is only set through the delete operation, not via this update. Audit trails use updated_at for tracking. Not-found errors occur if the id is invalid.
operations.summary: Update channel attributes in discussion_board_channels by id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The UUID of the channel to update, as stored in discussion_board_channels.id.

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the channel: one or more of code, name, or description (all schema fields).

responseBody.description: The updated channel record (all schema fields).

operations.specification: Soft delete a discussion board channel by id by updating the deleted_at field to the current timestamp in the discussion_board_channels table. This does not remove the row but marks it as deleted for audit and reversible moderation processes. Only the deleted_at field is set on this operation; all other fields remain unchanged. Requires administrator role.
operations.description: Deletes a channel by updating its deleted_at field to the current time (soft delete), marking the channel as deleted. The row remains in the database for future potential restoration or for audit purposes, as outlined in non-functional requirements. Attempts to delete a non-existent channel id will result in an error. The deletion is reversible (deleted_at can be cleared by a restore endpoint, not covered here). The operation guarantees compliance with audit and regulatory policies for reversibility and traceability. The operation only manipulates the deleted_at field; no non-schema fields are referenced. The response returns the channel's updated state after deletion, including the now-set deleted_at timestamp.
operations.summary: Soft delete a channel in discussion_board_channels by setting deleted_at.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of channel to soft delete (discussion_board_channels.id).

responseBody.description: Updated channel record with deleted_at set (or error if not found).

operations.specification: Create a new discussion board section in the discussion_board_sections table. A section is associated with a parent channel, with a unique code within the channel. The operation expects all schema fields: discussion_board_channel_id (foreign key), code (unique within channel), name, optional description, and audit timestamps. Soft deletion supported via deleted_at (not part of create). Unique constraint on (discussion_board_channel_id, code) enforced. Returns the created section record.
operations.description: This operation creates a new section under a given channel in the discussion_board_sections table. All required schema fields must be provided: a parent channel id (discussion_board_channel_id), unique section code (unique within channel), a user-facing section name, and an optional description. The created_at and updated_at timestamps are required by the schema and set to current time. Business and data integrity rules enforce that the code is unique among the same channel; violations return a unique constraint error. Only schema fields are accepted and returned; deleted_at is not set on create. This section can subsequently be referenced by discussions, posts, or moderation/admin tools. Audit and reversibility features leverage created_at/updated_at/deleted_at. Returns all details of the created section.
operations.summary: Create a new section in discussion_board_sections; section must be linked to channel.

requestBody.description: Required data for creating a section: channel id, code, name, optional description. All must match schema.

responseBody.description: The created section record as stored in the schema.

operations.specification: Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of sections from discussion_board_sections, with optional filtering by channel, code, name, description, and audit timestamps. Soft-deleted sections (deleted_at set) can be included/excluded based on request. Only schema fields are referenced for filter, pagination, or sorting. Results return only schema-defined fields. Intended for admin and moderation search or management views.
operations.description: Fetches a list of sections from the discussion_board_sections table, supporting search, filtering, and pagination using only schema-defined fields: discussion_board_channel_id, code, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Supports filtering by parent channel, partial name/code search, as well as time-range queries. By default, soft-deleted entries (deleted_at) are excluded unless specified otherwise in the request. Returns paginated results for admin screens or content management dashboards, with each section matching the schema definition. Only valid schema fields may be referenced in either request or response. Results array and pagination info are included in the response, no extra data outside the schema is included. Used for general admin listing, moderation, and content hierarchy management.
operations.summary: List and search sections from discussion_board_sections with pagination/filtering.

requestBody.description: Filter and pagination criteria for section search, all fields must exist in the schema.

responseBody.description: Paginated result with sections matching criteria, all fields from schema.

operations.specification: Fetch a single section from the discussion_board_sections table, by id, including all schema-defined details. Returns code, name, description, parent channel id, audit timestamps, and deleted_at as present. Only schema fields are included in both request and response. Intended for detailed section inspection or editing in admin dashboards.
operations.description: Retrieves a full section record identified by its id (UUID) from discussion_board_sections. Returns all schema fields: id, discussion_board_channel_id, code, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. If the id is not found, a not-found error is returned. Does not support or return any non-schema fields. Used for content structure inspection, pre-edit fetch, or detail view in admin tools. Logic assumes no additional or derived fields.
operations.summary: Get detailed information of a section in discussion_board_sections by id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the section to retrieve (discussion_board_sections.id).

responseBody.description: The complete section record as it appears in discussion_board_sections.

operations.specification: Update a section in discussion_board_sections, using the id to locate the record. Allows update of code, name, or description (the three atomic fields allowed by schema). Audit fields updated automatically. Only schema fields are updatable; changes to created_at or deleted_at are not supported. Returns the updated section record.
operations.description: This endpoint updates a section's code, name, or description using a PUT request with the section id and a body containing the fields to update. Only the schema-defined fields (code, name, description) are editable. The updated_at timestamp is set automatically to now. Attempting to change non-schema fields or to set a code that exists within the same channel will result in an error. Returns the section object after update, including all current field values from the schema, intended for admin and moderation uses. Does not interact with deleted_at except in separate soft delete flow.
operations.summary: Update one section in discussion_board_sections by id (atomic fields only).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the section to update (discussion_board_sections.id).

requestBody.description: Schema fields to update: code, name, or description (optionally any or all).

responseBody.description: The updated section record as stored in the schema.

operations.specification: Soft delete a section in discussion_board_sections by id. This sets deleted_at to the current timestamp. Record is not removed, supporting moderation reversibility and audit. Only the deleted_at field is set; other schema fields remain unchanged. Response returns all schema fields including new deleted_at.
operations.description: Performs a soft delete of a section: sets the deleted_at field to timestamp for reversible administrative deletion. The section remains in the DB; the operation sets only the deleted_at field. All other fields are preserved. Used for moderation, compliance, and reversible content structure management. Attempting to soft delete a non-existent section id results in error. Operation is for admin/moderator use only. The updated section is returned including new deleted_at.
operations.summary: Soft delete a section in discussion_board_sections by setting deleted_at.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the section to soft delete (discussion_board_sections.id).

responseBody.description: Updated section record with deleted_at timestamp set.

operations.specification: Create a new configuration property in discussion_board_configurations. Allows administrators to add new system settings or feature flags system-wide. Only schema fields allowed: key (unique), value, optional description, created_at, updated_at. No relations or soft deletion in schema. Returns the detail of the new configuration.
operations.description: This admin-only operation creates a system configuration property, for flags/settings like max_post_length or UI toggles. Requires a unique key, value string, and optional description; sets audit timestamps automatically. Only schema fields are accepted or returned (no relations). If creating a duplicate key, a unique constraint error is returned. Configuration is immediately available to system logic. Only atomic (non-derived, single-value) data is allowed in the value string.
operations.summary: Create a new configuration property in discussion_board_configurations.

requestBody.description: Unique key, value, and optional description for configuration.

responseBody.description: The configuration property as created in the schema.

operations.specification: List/search configuration properties from discussion_board_configurations, supporting filter by key, value, description, and audit timestamps. Paginates results for large config sets. No soft deletion; only schema fields for search and output. Intended for admin/config audit panel.
operations.description: Enables administrators to search, filter, and paginate through the platform's configuration properties in discussion_board_configurations. The request body details criteria for filtering by key, value, description, created_at, or updated_at. Returns all matched configuration properties, each strictly following the schema fields. Used for admin config panels, audit trails, and operational monitoring. No deleted_at field exists; all results are active configs. Pagination is included in the response, and each configuration property contains only actual schema fields.
operations.summary: List and search configuration properties in discussion_board_configurations with pagination/filtering.

requestBody.description: Filter/sort/pagination details (only actual schema fields) for config listing.

responseBody.description: Paginated config property set, where each matches schema fields.

operations.specification: GET: Retrieve a single configuration by ID from the discussion_board_configurations table. Returns full details for the configuration (including key, value, description, created_at, updated_at). Used by admins for viewing individual system settings.
operations.description: This operation fetches a configuration row from the discussion_board_configurations table. It returns all atomic fields present, including id (UUID), key, value, description (nullable), created_at and updated_at timestamps. As the entity does not include a deleted_at or soft delete field, configurations are only hard deleted and not hidden. This endpoint is intended for admin or system settings management, supporting platform configuration, system audits, or verifying feature flags. It checks existence by given UUID and delivers a complete object for display or admin-panel editing. Error handling includes 404 for not found, or permission denied if caller lacks appropriate role (e.g., administrator). This endpoint does not expose or permit modification, only pure viewing of the matched configuration object. Related endpoints enable list/search (PATCH) and CRUD operations for configurations.
operations.summary: Get configuration details by ID from discussion_board_configurations.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Target configuration's UUID

responseBody.description: Full configuration detail as stored in the database.

operations.specification: PUT: Update a system configuration by ID within the discussion_board_configurations table. Applies changes to key, value, description (if provided), enforcing system audit by updating the updated_at timestamp. Does NOT use soft deletes; any modifications are permanent and visible immediately to all users/systems depending on that setting.
operations.description: This endpoint allows administrators to update an existing configuration row by specifying its UUID. Only real fields in the schema—key, value, description—can be modified; created_at is unchanged, and updated_at is set to the current time. Since there is no deleted_at field, the system does not support soft delete for configurations, so all changes are permanent until the record is hard deleted. This operation is important for feature toggling, quota updating, or updating UI/system messages. Requires authentication and administrator role, as unauthorized configuration modification could impact critical system functionality. Related endpoints: GET for reading, PATCH for searching/listing, POST for creating. Validation enforces both field existence and uniqueness constraints (e.g., key must be unique).
operations.summary: Update a configuration entry by ID in discussion_board_configurations.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Target configuration's UUID

requestBody.description: New configuration data (key, value, optional description) for replacing fields in this configuration.

responseBody.description: Full updated configuration object after modification.

operations.specification: DELETE: Hard delete a system configuration by ID in the discussion_board_configurations table. Since no deleted_at field is present, deletion is irreversible and the item is permanently removed from the database.

Access control must ensure that only authorized users (e.g., the associated member, a moderator, or administrator) can view a member's search history. Moderation and privacy requirements dictate that search histories are not exposed publicly and that guests can only access their own (via actor_id/session).

When performing a search through this endpoint, clients may specify pagination details (offset, limit), sorting (by created_at, keyword, etc.), or provide advanced filters (e.g., search histories containing certain keywords, or within a specific date range/context). The response should include the requested page of full history records, each with all columns defined in the schema. For privacy/GDPR compliance, no deleted or anonymized records are exposed.

The endpoint requires authorization—only the subject user (actor), auditors, or administrators may access this endpoint. Guests may only access their own records, verified via session. If the specified id does not correspond to an existing record, or the requesting party does not have access rights, an appropriate not found or unauthorized error is returned.

No fields that do not exist in the schema (such as deleted_at, created_by) are referenced. Returns the actual, current record with all defined properties.

Prisma 스키마의 해당 컬럼에서 참조한 바와 같이 논리적인 반복을 방지하고, name과 별개로 원자적으로 관리됩니다.

예) 'eco', 'pol', 'law' 등의 내부 라우팅 주소로 쓰임.

name.description:

Full entity object for a discussion board thread, matching all fields in the Prisma schema's discussion_board_threads table.

Includes all properties: id, category and member linkage, title, pinned/closed state, full content, and audit timestamps (creation, update, deletion).

This is the central/top-level entity for discussions, as described in requirements Section 2 (Features & User Journeys). Used for detail views, thread lists, and programmatic introspection across API layers.

All IDs are UUIDs for consistent global linking and relationship representation.

Security: All response types must omit any actor authentication or sensitive PII that are forbidden by platform policy. Only public-facing system attributes included.

Aligns with standard IPage.IRequest pattern from the requirements analysis for API pagination and search.

Controls batch size for queries, helping to avoid excessive resource use during large search, list, or bulk fetches.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this moderation log record. This value serves as the primary key in the moderation logs table for the discussion board moderation domain. Automatically generated by the system at log creation. Reference: See 'id' in the Prisma schema for discussion_board_moderation_logs.

Serves for direct reference in audit trails, compliance checking, and API lookups. Must be present and unique for every moderation event record.

moderator_id.description:
UUID of the moderator who performed this action. Required. This foreign key references the moderator in the discussion_board_moderators table.

Business use: Identifies who enacted the moderation action, maintains role traceability, and ensures mod actions are auditable and not spoofed. Must always reference a valid, active moderator at the time of the event.

IModerationModerationLog.description:
Moderation Audit Log Entity

Represents a single immutable moderation action taken by a moderator in the discussion board system. This entity logs all audit attributes for compliance—who performed what action on which resource (thread, post, comment), the rationale for action, and when it took place. Ensures full business and regulatory traceability for every moderation event, as per requirements analysis and non-functional security/audit controls.

Reference: Prisma schema 'discussion_board_moderation_logs'.

IDiscussionBoardSubscription.description:
Represents a subscription relationship in the discussion board platform. This entity stores a user's (member's) subscription to a target resource, which enables them to receive notifications regarding updates or activity related to that target (such as threads, sections, tags, etc.).

This model enforces a normalized, atomic linkage between the subscriber and the subscribed resource. It is crucial for supporting the platform’s notification and alerting mechanisms as described in the requirements analysis. The schema enforces uniqueness for (member_id, target_type, target_id) to prevent duplicate notifications and manage resource-follow logic efficiently.

id.description:
Primary key. Uniquely identifies each subscription record. Used for all update, delete, and detail operations referencing a subscription.

This is a randomly generated UUID, ensuring global uniqueness.

Foreign key to the subscribing member (discussion_board_members.id). Indicates which user is following the resource for notification or activity tracking purposes.

Required. Used highly in filtering and subscriber personalized dashboards.

target_type.description:
The type of resource being followed/tested. For example, 'thread', 'section', 'tag', etc. This value is used to drive polymorphic notification logic.

Atomic and required for filtering, usability, and context-driven subscription delivery.

target_id.description:
The ID of the actual resource being followed (thread, section, tag, etc.). Its meaning is interpreted in conjunction with target_type.

Required. Used for notification dispatch and resource update queries.

Required for audit logging, time-based filtering, and administrative oversight.
